about: D11-2, the drills (docs/design/war.md §14.2; D-116). About forty drills in eight families; each names the branches it belongs to (no unit is offered a drill its branch has no use for), the war-map drill it feeds (60-unit-drill's GD.DRILLS key, read in battle), the ground it needs (open, forest, wall, river, coast), the skill its teacher must know, the tendency it mends and the task it prepares. Read by src/war/9999956-units (A.UNITS).

drills.name: Lock the wall
drills.desc: Shields overlapped, the rank shoulder to shoulder, and nobody steps out of it.

drills.name: Ground the butts
drills.desc: Spear butts set in the earth and the points low, so a horse runs onto them.

drills.name: Receive horse
drills.desc: Standing when the horses come: the one drill a foot company cannot learn on the day.

drills.name: Relieve the front rank
drills.desc: The second rank steps through and the first falls back to breathe, without a gap opening.

drills.name: The wedge
drills.desc: Riders in a point, the best at the front, the rest knee to knee behind.

drills.name: Charge knee to knee
drills.desc: A charge that arrives together, at one moment, not in a string.

drills.name: Rally after the charge
drills.desc: Coming back to the banner after the blow, while the enemy is still reeling.

drills.name: Dismount and hold
drills.desc: Knights on foot in a line, when the ground is wrong for horses.

drills.name: Hold the pursuit
drills.desc: Stopping at the trumpet, however good the chase looks.

drills.name: The screen
drills.desc: A thin line ahead of the column that sees and is not caught.

drills.name: Harry the column
drills.desc: Ride in, loose, ride off: the enemy's march made slow and angry.

drills.name: Feigned flight
drills.desc: Running away on purpose, and turning on the trumpet.

drills.name: Fight in pairs
drills.desc: Two men who cover each other, in broken ground or a wood.

drills.name: The volley on the horn
drills.desc: Every bow loosed at one call, so the arrows fall together.

drills.name: Ranging
drills.desc: Learning the long shot: where the arrows fall at two hundred paces, and three.

drills.name: Plant stakes
drills.desc: Sharpened stakes driven in before the line, which horses will not cross.

drills.name: Fall back behind the spears
drills.desc: Bowmen who come back through the spear wall in order, not in a crowd.

drills.name: Pavise and reload
drills.desc: Behind the big shield, winding the bow, and out again to shoot.

drills.name: The silent march
drills.desc: A night's march with no sound: muffled harness, no fire, no word.

drills.name: Hides
drills.desc: Lying up a day in a ditch or a thicket, watching the road.

drills.name: Reading tracks
drills.desc: How many passed, how long ago, horse or foot, and how tired.

drills.name: The night knife
drills.desc: Taking a sentry, or a prisoner, without waking the camp.

drills.name: Drawing the ground
drills.desc: Bringing back the ground on paper: the fords, the woods, the high places.

drills.name: The ladder
drills.desc: Carrying a ladder to a wall under arrows, and up it.

drills.name: The sap
drills.desc: A trench dug forward to the wall, and a mine under it.

drills.name: The ram and the tower
drills.desc: Building and pushing the great engines up to a gate.

drills.name: Bridging
drills.desc: A river crossed in a day: boats lashed, planks laid, the carts over.

drills.name: Camp and ditch
drills.desc: A ditch and a bank round the camp every night, dug in an hour.

drills.name: Pace and intervals
drills.desc: Marching at one pace with the gaps kept, so the column does not bunch and string out.

drills.name: The forced march
drills.desc: Fifty kilometres in a day, and fit to fight at the end of it.

drills.name: Form from the march
drills.desc: Out of the column and into the line before the enemy is on you.

drills.name: Foraging
drills.desc: Finding bread and fodder in a land that hides them.

drills.name: Loading and the wagon line
drills.desc: Wagons loaded right, the line kept, nothing left behind.

drills.name: Boarding
drills.desc: Over the rail with grapnel and axe.

drills.name: Rowing in stroke
drills.desc: Oars together, so the galley answers.

drills.name: The landing
drills.desc: Out of the boats and formed on the shore before the enemy comes down.
